messages:
sam: Quick sync — we're planning to stop special-casing the legacy `X-Client-Version` header in the public gateway (target: API v3). Proposal: deploy a tiny translator sidecar that normalizes legacy headers and request shape into the canonical form so backend services can assume new contract. Thoughts on perf and operational complexity?

maria: Performance is my #1 concern. How much latency are we adding at p50/p99? If it's per-request sync hop we need numbers. Also where does auth happen — before or after the translator?

aj: My 2c: keep auth verification upstream in the gateway. Translator should only rewrite headers/body, not revalidate tokens. We can implement translator as an Envoy filter (Lua) or small Go sidecar. Envoy filter = lower overhead, sidecar = easier to iterate.

sam: Good call on auth. I was thinking translator runs adjacent to the gateway process so it sees raw request pre-auth. But better: do auth first then translator (so rewrites are internal). That means translator must preserve signature semantics or rewrite token mapping if needed.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: translator-service v0.1 deployed to staging cluster-3 for perf tests :rocket:

julie: If we go Envoy Lua we can do something like:
```
filters:
  - name: envoy.filters.http.lua
    typed_config:
      "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.lua.v3.Lua
      inline_code: |
        function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
          local v = request_handle:headers():get("X-Client-Version")
          if v and v:match("^legacy_") then
            request_handle:headers():replace("X-RI-Client", "normalized")
            request_handle:headers():remove("X-Client-Version")
          end
        end
```
This keeps latency ~sub-ms in our tests.

maria: Nice. Two operational notes: 1) Provide per-tenant toggle (some enterprise customers depend on old header semantics), 2) Emit a compatibility metric we can break down by tenant and header variant.

aj: Also watch caching semantics. If we canonicalize headers, existing cache keys may change and hit rates could drop. We should key caches with canonicalized header value to avoid cache duplication.

sam: Rollout plan suggestion: (1) deploy translator in passive mode (no-op + telemetry) for 48h, (2) enable rewrite behind tenant opt-in for canaries, (3) global enable for non-enterprise tenants and publish deprecation notice 60 days, (4) remove legacy handling from gateway.

julie: Add to (1) a response header `X-RI-Compat: translator=1` so we can surface to customers/telemetry. Also add a telemetry counter `compat.rewrites` with labels `tenant` and `variant`.

maria: For Dedicated/Private customers we should make this an explicit config toggle in their control plane. Don't auto-flip.

aj: One more: plan for signature-propagation cases where clients sign a header payload. We need a deterministic canonicalization algorithm and include it in the RFC/deprecation doc so integrators can update.

sam: Agreed. Action items: julie -> prototype Envoy filter and perf numbers (due EOD Friday); aj -> cache-keying plan and docs; maria -> contact top 5 enterprise customers and draft toggle policy; i'll write deprecation timeline and announcement draft. We'll review Monday. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
